TOP OF BOOK

  • US CPI JUNE 2026 [DELTA ▼] — Headline CPI -0.4% MoM / +3.5% YoY; core flat MoM / +2.6% YoY — materially better than all consensus estimates across the board.
    • Vs. baseline: CPI -0.4% on the month; annual rate 3.5%. Consensus was -0.2% MoM and 3.8% YoY. Core flat MoM vs. 0.2% expected; 12-month core 2.6% vs. 2.9% forecast. Double miss to the soft side on both headline and core. This is the most relevant data point for global rates in weeks.
    • Read: The miss was driven entirely by energy — the energy index shed 5.7% over the month, its steepest one-month retreat since April 2020. The relief is real but structurally fragile: today's CPI does not reflect the recent energy-price rebound driven by renewed US-Iran military escalation; Brent climbed to a one-month high above $86/bbl on Tuesday after the US reinstated a naval blockade on Iranian vessels in the Strait of Hormuz. Treasury yields fell sharply on the report; Fed hike odds for September dropped to 63% from >75% a day earlier. For European financials: softer US inflation prints through the summer would reduce the risk of imported inflationary pressure into the eurozone and ease the case for further ECB tightening, supporting European bank bond books and reducing NII ceiling compression risk. But the oil re-escalation already running in parallel caps how far this repricing goes. Near-term rates leg: long front-end Bunds / OATs on this read; but a short-duration hedge on the energy re-escalation tail is still needed. No action on equities — the transmission is rate-book not earnings for European banks in this quarter.
    • Sources: BLS CPI release | CNBC
  • GOLDMAN SACHS (GS) [DELTA ▲] — Record Q2 2026: revenue $20.3bn, EPS $20.98 — beat consensus by ~46% on EPS and ~26% on revenue.
    • Vs. baseline: GS delivered its strongest quarterly performance on record; EPS $20.98 vs. analyst consensus of $14.48, revenue $20.3bn. Stock +7.66% on the day. Beat magnitude is extreme, not incremental.
    • Read: Global Banking & Markets net revenues $15.5bn, up 53% YoY; equity underwriting up 130%, debt underwriting up 75%. ROTE 25.5% for the quarter. The relevance for European banks is the wholesale banking read-through: a record quarter for US market-makers driven by M&A, equities and AI-financing validates the same tailwind that will benefit Barclays CIB and BNP CIB into their H1 results this month. Backlog at a five-year high; full-year alternatives fundraising guidance >$125bn. Fee and spread income at this scale confirms the durability of the IB revenue recovery, a direct positive for European CIB NII and fee analogues. Equity leg: positive read-through for Barclays (CIB-heavy) and SocGen; less direct for retail-anchored names. Watch the Barclays 28 July H1 print as a direct test of whether this translates to European rates. MONITOR.
    • Sources: Investing.com | Yahoo Finance / Quartz
  • JPMORGAN CHASE (JPM) [DELTA ▲] — Q2 record net income $21.2bn / EPS $7.70 reported (adj. $6.14 excl. Visa gain); revenue $58bn, up 27% YoY.
    • Vs. baseline: Net income $21.2bn (incl. $4.6bn Visa gain); adj. EPS $6.14 vs. $5.74 consensus (+7%); every line of business posted record revenue. NII guidance lifted. Full-year NII outlook raised to ~$105.5bn from $103bn.
    • Read: Equity Markets revenue +86% YoY to $6bn; total Markets $12.1bn, topping the prior record. IB fees +30% to $3.3bn, highest since 2021. NII guidance upgrade is the critical European read-through: it confirms that higher-for-longer rates are still flowing through loan books and accreting into NII — a positive for European bank NII analogues (ING, Santander, HSBC). Dimon's warning on geopolitics, inflation and "tectonic plates" below the surface is consistent with the oil re-escalation and active US-Iran military exchange underway in real time. MONITOR for European NII beat expectations at upcoming results.
    • Sources: Yahoo Finance / Quartz | AlphaStreet
  • CITIGROUP (C) [DELTA ▲] — Q2 beat but stock -4% on H2 expense guidance.
    • Vs. baseline: EPS $3.15 vs. $2.73 consensus (+15%); revenue $24.8bn, up 14% YoY, best in a decade. Despite the beat, shares fell 4.16% as investors digested management's decision to maintain full-year return guidance and signal increased H2 investment spending.
    • Read: RoTCE hit 13% — upper boundary of the 2027–28 target range — but equities growth trailed larger rivals; CFO acknowledged Citi had "not moved quickly enough" to build its equities franchise. The guidance-hold despite an over-earning H1 is the negative signal: management is front-loading costs, compressing the H2 NII and earnings path. Secondary read-through for European universal banks: markets will now more closely scrutinise any European name that beats but simultaneously signals elevated reinvestment spend, with NII guidance held rather than raised. MONITOR on Barclays/BNP cost trajectory.
    • Sources: Quartz | Investing.com

BY NAME / THEME

  • UNICREDIT / COMMERZBANK (UCG.MI / CBK.DE) [IN LINE] — Tender offer closed: UniCredit at ~47.6% economic / 49.65% voting stake; ECB control determination pending.
    • Vs. baseline: UniCredit is set to control almost 48% of Commerzbank's shares; taking into account treasury shares (no votes), the Italian firm will have 49.65% of votes once physical settlement completes — which could take several months. Commerzbank states less than 2% of institutional and retail investors tendered; the low acceptance rate reflects independent shareholder preference for Commerzbank's stand-alone strategy over the offer terms.
    • Read: Excluding treasury shares UniCredit is at 49.7% voting stake — a level Orcel has said is likely to prompt the ECB to declare it has de facto control, which would force minority consolidation and be "a major blow to its capital reserves," with material CET1 dilution affecting funding costs and capital ratios. Options ahead: amending swap contracts to reach ~59%, buying more on the open market once regulatory approval clears, or negotiating directly. The ECB control determination is the key binary — if triggered, UniCredit faces forced minority consolidation with significant CET1 dilution. CBK equity: independent stand-alone strategy now embedded; the 17% RoE by 2028 target is the new trading anchor. UCG equity and AT1: watch for any signal on capital strategy if ECB declares control. DIG IN on ECB ruling timeline.
    • Sources: Bloomberg | Commerzbank | Reuters/Business Recorder
  • BANK OF AMERICA (BAC) [DELTA ▲] — Q2 beat: NI $9.1bn, EPS $1.21 vs $1.13 est; NII $16bn (+9% YoY); ROTE 17%.
    • Vs. baseline: Net income $9.1bn, up 27% YoY; revenue $31.6bn, up 15%; EPS $1.21. NII $15,997m vs $14,670m a year ago.
    • Read: Equities trading +70% to $3.6bn; FICC +9% to $3.5bn. NII growth of 9% YoY is the European read-through — confirms that the rate environment is still accreting into bank income statements via loan repricing and deposit mix, validating NII-growth themes at HSBC, Barclays, and Santander. Net charge-off ratio fell to 0.47% from 0.55% — credit quality holding, which is the key watch for European consumer-facing banks. MONITOR.
    • Sources: BofA Investor Relations | Quartz
  • BARCLAYS (BARC.L) [NEW] — Rosen Law Firm investor notice filed (US-listed ADR, BCS); no new litigation announced. H1 results 28 July.
    • Vs. baseline: The Rosen Law Firm GlobeNewswire notice (from supplied feed) appears to be a standard plaintiff firm solicitation, not a newly filed case. Barclays H1 2026 results scheduled 28 July; Q3 results 22 October. No material new litigation development identified.
    • Read: The US law-firm solicitation is immaterial in isolation. The real catalyst is the 28 July H1 print — the GS / JPM / BofA beats set a high bar for CIB. Barclays' structural hedge book and UK mortgage repricing (rates cut up to 66bps across residential ranges, effective 9 July) are the NII swing factors to watch: mortgage spread compression could partially offset the rate-accrual benefit on the hedge book. Equity: hold position into print; any miss on CIB relative to the US comp will be penalised. MONITOR.
    • Sources: Barclays IR
  • PRIVATE CREDIT (SECTOR THEME) [DELTA ▼] — US direct-lending volume -55% QoQ in Q2; $14bn trapped in redemption queues; HSBC halts lending to riskier funds.
    • Vs. baseline: US direct-lending volume fell ~55% QoQ to $33.6bn in Q2, the lowest since Q2 2023; deal count fell to 154 from 217. Separately, HSBC is halting lending to riskier private credit funds following high-profile corporate bankruptcies; the bank informed clients it will not renew certain credit facilities or provide back leverage. And as H2 gets underway, direct lenders are facing relentless redemption pressure, with $14bn trapped.
    • Read: Three concurrent signals: volume collapse, bank back-leverage withdrawal (HSBC), and redemption gating. The HSBC move is the most significant for European bank credit exposure — it signals that at least one major European GSIB has moved from passive concern to active risk-reduction on private credit counterparty exposure, directly tightening its funding supply to the sector and reducing fee income from NAV-financing facilities. Watch for similar moves at BNP, Deutsche, and ING where NAV-financing and subscription-line exposure exists. For European bank equity: the credit-quality transmission channel is the risk — if private-credit fund stress forces asset sales into a rising-rate/tighter-spread environment, mark-to-market losses could spill back onto bank balance sheets via CLO residuals or warehouse facilities. Leg: credit (senior non-preferred spreads of banks with private-credit exposure) is where the risk shows first. DIG IN on HSBC / BNP exposure sizing.
    • Sources: Reuters via 93.3 The Drive | Bloomberg | Bloomberg
  • ECB DIGITAL EURO PILOT — 36 PSPs SELECTED (ECB) [IN LINE] — ECB announces 36 payment service providers chosen for the digital euro pilot; pilot launch H2 2027.
    • Vs. baseline: The ECB has selected 36 PSPs from across the euro area for the digital euro pilot; starting H2 2027, the 12-month exercise will take place at the ECB and 19 national central banks. ECB aims to be ready for first issuance in 2029, assuming the legislative process is completed by end of 2026.
    • Read: Operationally on-track per prior guidance. The 36-PSP selection confirms broad industry participation, reducing tail risk of a project abandonment. The medium-term read for payments incumbents (Worldline, Adyen, Nexi) is structurally disruptive — a pan-European CBDC rail directly competes with card-scheme and acquirer economics, threatening interchange and acquiring spread income. The European Parliament ECON vote on the Single Currency Package earlier this month cleared a key political gate. No immediate positioning consequence — the 2029 issuance date is far enough out to be irrelevant for 12–18 month price targets. MONITOR for legislative completion risk at year-end.
    • Sources: ECB Press Release | Cipollone interview, Jornal de Negócios

CREDIT CORNER

  • ECB RATE PATH — JULY HOLD NOW 88% PRICED [DELTA ▲] — Post-CPI and post-Sintra dovish signals, markets now price 88% hold on 23 July; September hike probability collapsing.
    • Vs. baseline: Pricing implies 88% probability the ECB holds at 2.25% on 23 July. The September hike that looked like a coin-flip a month ago now looks unlikely on current data. The June hike is starting to look like a one-and-done. Eurozone inflation fell to 2.8% in June from 3.2% in May, undercutting the case for further ECB hikes. Context: markets had previously seen 70% probability of a September hike following renewed US-Iran oil price surge driven by active US military strikes and Iranian retaliatory strikes in the strait.
    • Read: The June +25bp hike (deposit rate now 2.25%) looks increasingly terminal unless Brent sustains above $90. The rapid repricing from "three hikes in 2026" to "one-and-done" is a major shift in the NII terminal rate assumption for European banks — it caps the NII upgrade cycle but at the same time reduces provisioning pressure and borrower stress. Net: modest equity negative vs. the prior pricing (NII ceiling lower), but credit spread positive (less tightening = less credit stress). For AT1 market: reduces new supply risk premium from forced issuance at higher rates, supporting spread compression. Front-end Bund yields — watch the 2-year on any Cipollone/Lagarde comment ahead of 23 July. MONITOR into ECB meeting.
    • Sources: Cambridge Currencies / Market Pricing | Trading Economics
  • BRENT CRUDE — $85–86/bbl, US-IRAN RE-ESCALATION [DELTA ▲] — Brent at 1-month high, +~10% in 48 hours, as Trump reinstates Hormuz blockade.
    • Vs. baseline: Brent climbed above $85 on Tuesday, gaining >10% for the week, after the US reinstated a naval blockade on Iranian vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz effective 4pm ET Tuesday. US CENTCOM announced strikes on Iran for a third consecutive day; Iran's IRGC struck two oil supertankers in the strait and launched missile and drone strikes against US assets in Kuwait and Bahrain.
    • Read: The June CPI relief was built entirely on the energy disinflation of a prior ceasefire period — that ceasefire has broken down, with the US conducting strikes and Iran retaliating. The July CPI (released mid-August) will capture this re-escalation. For European banks: (1) higher energy inflation re-loads the ECB hiking cycle risk, directly threatening NII ceiling assumptions by pushing the terminal rate higher and counteracting the rate-path repricing above; (2) sovereign-bank loop: peripheral sovereigns (Italy, Spain, Greece) face larger fiscal drag from energy costs — BTP-Bund spreads are the watch; (3) energy-sector loan quality — European banks with oil-sector or shipping-sector exposure benefit from higher collateral values but face heightened geopolitical credit risk. Net positioning: short front-end OATs / BTPs as a hedge against the re-escalation scenario; the rates-vol environment argues for holding these hedges through the 23 July ECB. DIG IN on BTP-Bund spread trajectory.
    • Sources: Al Jazeera
